messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
Ayush Jain
ayush jain... classic name, probably heard "ayush from delhi?" a million times. where you working these days?
hey ayush, was just thinking about your background - what's your current company and how many years you've been there?
American Express, 3 years

american express... that's serious fintech. building payment infrastructure or stuck in the corporate maze? 

found you on linkedin - sr manager, marketing & product analytics. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/ayush-jain-b0991822

I work with spend analytics and forecasting
  No, that's not me

spend analytics and forecasting... so you're the guy telling amex how much money people will blow next quarter. that's solid data work.

can't find the right ayush jain on linkedin with your details. drop your linkedin url or send me your resume - need one of these to find you proper roles
https://www.linkedin.com/in/ayushj0907

ayush jain at american express... 3 years deep in the credit card empire, probably seen every spending pattern from chai addicts to crypto bros. what made you stick with amex for this long? most people bounce after 2 years.

User's LinkedIn Profile Context:
**EXECUTIVE SUMMARY**
Ayush Jain is a Data Science Analyst who works with transactional data to deliver actionable insights. He is currently with American Express in New Delhi, India.

**ROLE-BY-ROLE**
*   American Express ([Start date not specified]) – [Role title not specified] – [Responsibilities not listed]

**EDUCATION HIGHLIGHTS**
*   [No education information listed]

**CERTIFICATIONS**
*   Academy Accreditation - Databricks Lakehouse Fundamentals (Databricks, Issued May 2024)

ceo and cfo exposure in 3 years... that's actually solid. most analysts are stuck talking to middle management forever. sql, python, pyspark, bigquery - you've got the full data stack down.

but here's the thing - you sound comfortable. maybe too comfortable. how long you been working total across all companies?
Almost 4.5 years

4.5 years total, 3 at amex... so you jumped ship once early and then settled in. smart move actually - most people job hop too much or stay too long.

with that sql/python/bigquery combo and senior leadership exposure, you're probably ready for something bigger. what kind of role you looking for next?
Any data centric role, analytics mostly but financial modelling and forecasting is okay too. I would want to work for company that's generally known for paying high

analytics + financial modeling + "companies that pay high"... i see you're done with the corporate "we're a family" nonsense and want actual money.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
Open for remote, bangalore and gurgaon
4.5 years experience + analytics/financial modeling + remote/bangalore/gurgaon + high paying companies... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
Yes
cool. just ping me when you're ready to talk specifics or see what's out there.
Nothing
Is everything okay?

everything's good - just getting your profile ready on my end. you'll see roles when my team sends something that fits.

so... what's the actual worry?
Hi
Hi tal

hey boss

what's up?
I'm good, just finished up with work
nice. how's the amex grind been lately?
Interesting but strict work. Lots to do

that tracks. fintech's always either chaos or bureaucracy.

what's making you want to look around? just growth or something else?
More interesting work for the most part. I've created a lot for a lot of teams here. I want to do the same in other companies. And the possibility of a nice pay bump

makes sense. you've built systems that work, now you want to build somewhere else and get paid properly for it.

what's your current comp? and what would make you actually move?
I would consider switching for 45L base/fixed with extra stock options

45L base + stock... that's ambitious for 4.5 YOE but not impossible at the right places.

what's your current base at amex? just so i know what kind of jump we're talking.
I'm at 35L base

35L → 45L base is a solid jump. plus stock on top... you're aiming for the top tier companies.

remote okay? or you want bangalore/gurgaon?

Considering my current base, jump to 45L doesn't seem like a lot. That's the minimum I'm expecting. I know companies offer more than that too. I recognise you have to be top of your game for those opportunities and that's where I consider myself to be
  I'm fine with remote. Bangalore or Gurgaon is fine too

i like the confidence. you're right - 45L base is doable at the right places for someone who's actually good.

what kind of companies are you thinking? fintech? product? something else?
Fintech or product both sound good. Financial companies like JP Morgan or Morgan Stanley. Tech heavy companies like Uber, google, microsoft, Disney

got it. you're aiming for the big leagues - banks and tech giants.

i'll keep an eye out for analytics roles at those places. anything specific you want to avoid?
Not really. I'll take them all

alright. i'm locked in. you'll see roles when something actually fits.

btw what's making you want to leave amex anyway? just the money or something else?
Nothing's making me leave. The culture and work is great here. I just don't feel challenged enough and I'm curious about companies that work faster

that's the real reason right there. you want that startup energy but at a place that can actually pay you.

i'll look for roles at fast-moving teams within those big companies. the ones that feel like startups but have the bank account to match.

you're all set. i'll slide roles when they're good.

paypal's looking for a senior data analyst in chennai

tier 1 fintech, exactly the kind of high-paying company you mentioned

hybrid setup - 3 days office, 2 days flexible
